articles.title: How Do Companies Cover Natural Disaster Risks in the Face of Climate Change?
articles.summary: MAPFRE examines how rising wildfire, flood and hurricane risk is reducing insurance availability in exposed regions. It describes insurance and public-private risk-sharing as mechanisms for compensating losses and supporting recovery from natural disasters.

articles.title: Insurers: Climate Risk Disclosures Today, Scenario Testing Tomorrow
articles.summary: McDermott reviews climate-risk reporting requirements for US insurers and the move toward regulatory scenario testing. It contrasts US disclosure practice with European financial-risk analysis and describes a three-year US scenario-testing trial.

articles.title: Climate Change Presses On: Devastating Wildfires and Intense Thunderstorms Exacerbate Losses for Insurers
articles.summary: Munich Re reports that insured natural-disaster losses again exceeded US$100 billion in 2025. Wildfires, flooding and severe thunderstorms accounted for almost all insured losses, while 17,200 people died in natural disasters.

articles.title: Lower Losses, Growing Risks: The Natural Disaster Review for the First Half of 2026
articles.summary: Munich Re estimates first-half 2026 natural-disaster losses at nearly US$112 billion, of which US$44 billion was insured, leaving a 60% insurance gap. The review also highlights earthquakes, record heatwaves and the prospect of a strong El Niño.

articles.title: From Risk to Resilience: How States Are Approaching Insurance and Climate Risk in 2026
articles.summary: NCEL describes worsening US homeowners-insurance affordability and insurer withdrawals as climate risk rises. It presents Colorado HB25-1182 as a model that has inspired bipartisan state legislation focused on transparency and resilience.

articles.title: Parametric Insurance for Climate Change Adaptation
articles.summary: The Observer Research Foundation examines parametric insurance as a climate-adaptation instrument that makes predefined, fixed payments when natural-resource flows reach agreed thresholds. It illustrates the mechanism with a rainfall-triggered hydropower policy and notes that payouts usually cover only part of actual losses.

articles.title: Fight Against Climate Change: ARC Now Covers Floods
articles.summary: African Risk Capacity launched Africa's first sovereign parametric flood-insurance policy, with Madagascar becoming the first subscribing country in January 2026. The product is intended to strengthen anticipatory, Africa-led climate-risk financing.

articles.title: Insured Losses from Natural Catastrophes Reached $44 Billion in H1 2026: Munich Re
articles.summary: Reinsurance News reports Munich Re's estimate of US$44 billion in insured natural-catastrophe losses against nearly US$112 billion in total losses in the first half of 2026. The resulting 60% insurance gap remained despite losses being below recent averages.

articles.title: Swiss Re sees claims from natural catastrophes rising in 2026
articles.summary: Swiss Re estimates that insured losses from natural catastrophes will reach about US$148 billion in 2026, based on the long-term average, and could rise to US$320 billion in a severe scenario. It says 2025's lower losses reflected favourable variability rather than an easing of underlying risk.

articles.title: SEARCA, EcoSecurities and UPLBFI Strengthen PCIC Capacity for Data-Driven Corn Insurance
articles.summary: SEARCA, EcoSecurities and UPLBFI held a workshop for the Philippine Crop Insurance Corporation on data-driven parametric crop insurance for corn. The training covered loss modelling, climate risk and GIS-based payout systems to support climate-resilient agricultural finance.

articles.title: The Growth of Parametric Insurance
articles.summary: The SOA article explains how parametric policies operate and how their design, pricing and reserving differ from traditional indemnity insurance. It reviews current applications, anticipated market growth and considerations for general-insurance actuaries.

articles.title: Climate Risk: Catastrophe Planning and Financial Modeling for Retirement
articles.summary: This SOA essay examines how climate catastrophes affect retirement planning, with older and disabled people particularly vulnerable during evacuation, relocation and recovery. It considers catastrophe exposure, insurance, financial modelling and household preparedness for retirees.

articles.title: Beyond the Threshold: An Actuarial Perspective on Evaluating Climate Adaptation in an Age of Escalating Disasters
articles.summary: The essay argues that non-stationary, compounding climate disasters challenge actuarial reliance on historical experience and stable distributions. It calls for actuaries to evaluate adaptation interventions systematically alongside catastrophe modelling and risk pricing.

articles.title: Assessing the Applicability of the Actuaries Climate Index Within a Weather Derivatives Framework
articles.summary: The research assesses whether the Actuaries Climate Index can support a weather-derivatives framework. It studies weather-based indices and a modelling approach for transferring risk associated with climate and weather variability.

articles.title: Climate Scenarios to Actuarial Assumptions: A Practitioner's Framework
articles.summary: The SOA research call seeks a practical framework for translating NGFS, IPCC and IEA scenario variables into actuarial assumptions. It targets pricing, reserving and solvency analysis under IFRS S2, ORSA and insurer climate-risk management.

articles.title: Climate Change Resilience and Adaptation Initiatives and Programs: A Collection of Essays
articles.summary: The SOA collection examines programmes that build resilience, compare expected costs and savings, and measure adaptation performance. Its essays include real-option evaluation, quantitative effectiveness frameworks and uses of artificial intelligence and actuarial techniques.

articles.title: ISSB Developments, March 2026: Latest Progress on Nature-related Disclosures
articles.summary: The article explains the ISSB's renaming of its BEES project to Nature-related Disclosures and its broader coverage of nature-related risks and opportunities. It describes planned compatibility with IFRS S1, IFRS S2, TNFD, SASB, GRI and ESRS and progress toward an exposure draft.

articles.title: SCIPP: Climate Science Data for Southern US States
articles.summary: SCIPP supplies climate data, planning tools and engagement support to communities in the south-central United States. Its work helps local leaders assess weather and climate risks, reduce disaster impacts and plan with hazard information.

articles.title: May 2026 – Where does the world stand on ISSB adoption?
articles.summary: S&P Global reviews the global uptake of IFRS S1 and IFRS S2: as of 22 April 2026, 28 jurisdictions had adopted the standards and 12 more planned to do so. It examines jurisdiction-specific approaches to climate disclosures, including GHG emissions, physical and transition risks, Scope 3 emissions, climate-resilience assessment and scenario analysis.

articles.title: Swiss Re Group
articles.summary: Swiss Re's corporate homepage identifies the group as a global provider of reinsurance and insurance focused on resilience. It serves as the entry point to the group's insurance, reinsurance and risk resources.

articles.title: Natural Catastrophes in 2025: The Persistent Rise of Wildfire and Storm Risk
articles.summary: Swiss Re Institute reports US$107 billion of insured natural-catastrophe losses in 2025 and a continuing 5–7% long-term real growth trend. Secondary perils generated 92% of losses, while its 2026 peak-loss scenario reaches US$320 billion.

articles.title: Natural Catastrophes in 2025: When Exposure Outpaces Adaptation
articles.summary: Swiss Re's sigma research examines increasing wildfire and storm risk and the insured losses recorded in 2025. It emphasizes adaptation and insurance innovation as responses when growing exposure outpaces resilience measures.

articles.title: First-half 2026 Insured Catastrophe Losses: Below Trend, Rising Risks
articles.summary: Swiss Re Institute estimates global insured natural-catastrophe losses of US$42 billion in the first half of 2026, below the US$66 billion long-term trend. The analysis cautions that underlying catastrophe risks continue to rise despite the below-trend period.

articles.title: Natural Catastrophes: The US$424 Billion Protection Gap and Adaptation to Counter Growing Exposure
articles.summary: Swiss Re Institute describes a US$424 billion natural-catastrophe protection gap and links it to growing exposure. The page presents adaptation as a means of reducing risk that remains uninsured.

articles.title: Remarks at the Press Launch of the Financing for Sustainable Development Report 2026
articles.summary: UN DESA presents the 2026 report as a call to implement the Sevilla Commitment amid widening development-finance gaps, falling aid and rising debt-service burdens. It calls for larger, affordable and long-term investment to deliver the Sustainable Development Goals.

articles.title: Unlocking climate finance
articles.summary: UNDP presents the Adaptation Finance Strategy Guideline, a practical framework for governments to mobilize and align finance with adaptation investments in National Adaptation Plans and Nationally Determined Contributions. The guideline uses a modular approach for governments, development partners and the private sector to strengthen financing systems and scale investment around national adaptation priorities.

articles.title: Powering Health and Climate Security in BARMM: UNDP, Japan, and Lanao del Sur Advance Renewable Energy for Resilient Communities
articles.summary: The RE3ACHS project installed 271 kWp of hybrid solar photovoltaic capacity across four health facilities in Lanao del Sur to strengthen reliable healthcare, energy security and climate resilience. The initiative also trained health staff and solar installers, supported local energy planning and aims to reduce diesel dependence and greenhouse gas emissions.

articles.title: Climate Finance Dialogues 2026 convenes partners in Rome to advance climate investment opportunities across Africa
articles.summary: Climate Finance Dialogues 2026 brings governments, project developers, development finance institutions and investors together to move African climate and energy projects toward bankability and implementation. Through PISTA and Energy for Growth in Africa, the programme connects project preparation with financing for renewable energy, resilient infrastructure, clean mobility, agriculture and water systems.

articles.title: UNDP and IAI convene high-level roundtable in Rome to advance climate and development finance partnerships
articles.summary: UNDP and Istituto Affari Internazionali convened public, private and financial-sector participants in Rome to strengthen coordination for climate and development finance, with a focus on Africa. The roundtable examined bankable climate-resilient project pipelines, access to public and private investment, technical assistance and institutional partnerships.

articles.title: The next generation of climate peacebuilders
articles.summary: UNDP shows how young people in fragile and conflict-affected settings are developing responses to overlapping climate, peace and security challenges. Examples from Egypt, South Sudan, Tanzania and Lebanon cover floodwater harvesting, climate-resilient agriculture, youth peacebuilding, alternative livelihoods and climate-information integrity.

articles.title: The planet is in crisis. Our response must rise to the moment.
articles.summary: UNDP presents land degradation, biodiversity decline and increasingly extreme climate conditions as interconnected environmental crises affecting food, water, livelihoods and stability. It highlights the three 2026 environmental conferences—UNCCD COP17, the UN Biodiversity Conference COP17 and UN Climate Change Conference COP31—as opportunities to advance land restoration, biodiversity protection and climate action.

articles.title: Climate Finance
articles.summary: UNEP supports governments and financial institutions in mobilizing public and private finance for Paris Agreement mitigation and adaptation goals. Its work integrates climate risk into planning and promotes resilient, inclusive and low-carbon development.

articles.title: Net-Zero Export Credit Agencies Alliance
articles.summary: The UN-convened alliance brings together public export-credit institutions committed to supporting the transition to net-zero economies by 2050. It focuses on aligning export finance with decarbonisation.

articles.title: UNEP FI Climate Pathways Navigator
articles.summary: UNEP FI's tool gives financial institutions direct access to climate-scenario data for science-based decisions. It helps users navigate pathway information needed to assess climate-related risks and strategies.

articles.title: European Sustainability Reporting Standards
articles.summary: UNEP FI outlines the European Sustainability Reporting Standards in the context of the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive, which entered into force in January 2023. The resource addresses interoperability and companies' social and environmental reporting obligations.

articles.title: Climate Change: Risk Management in the Banking Sector Online Course
articles.summary: UNEP FI's online course covers climate-related risks and opportunities for financial institutions. The training incorporates climate-disclosure recommendations and practical risk-management approaches for banking professionals.

articles.title: Applying Taxonomies to Scale Climate-resilient Investment Opportunities in Asia-Pacific
articles.summary: The UNEP FI webinar introduces an Adaptation Finance Taxonomy Playbook for identifying, assessing and scaling adaptation finance. It addresses financial institutions seeking credible investment classifications amid rising heat, flood, drought, storm and sea-level risks in Asia-Pacific.

articles.title: What is parametric insurance and how is it building climate resilience?
articles.summary: Parametric policies pay when measurable weather conditions cross agreed thresholds, enabling faster and more flexible payments while covering some climate risks that conventional indemnity insurance may leave unprotected. Satellite and AI-enabled products can expand coverage, but threshold-dependent design can leave losses unpaid and increasingly frequent climate events may challenge product sustainability.

articles.title: The role of insurance in building resilience across the energy-water-climate nexus
articles.summary: Insurance de-risks and underwrites private investment across the energy-water-climate nexus and can move beyond post-disaster payouts to finance resilience before shocks occur. The article calls for risk reduction at source, pre-disaster investment, fair risk sharing, better data paired with public decisions and equitable risk-based pricing, illustrating these principles with peatland flood protection and parametric cover for heat and flooding.

articles.title: Systemic risk is the hidden tax on growth. Here's how insurance can help build economic resilience
articles.summary: Systemic risk arising from climate volatility, geopolitical fragmentation, technological disruption and public-health crises behaves like a hidden tax by raising investment costs, discouraging innovation and transmitting shocks through interconnected systems. Insurance can convert uncertainty into resilience through risk quantification, pooling and transfer, advanced modelling and early warning, adaptation investment and public-private risk sharing.

articles.title: How avoided emissions can help unlock investment in low-carbon innovation
articles.summary: Avoided emissions compare the greenhouse-gas impact of a low-carbon solution with a scenario in which that solution is absent, capturing customer-side reductions not fully recognized by Scope 1–3 accounting. They should be reported separately from GHG inventories; broader use in investment and lending could reward low-carbon technologies, but methodologies still require clearer baselines, reference scenarios, attribution and calculation disclosure.

articles.title: Leaders should plan for colliding risks, not isolated crises. Here's why
articles.summary: The article warns that severe corporate disruption can emerge when geopolitical, cyber, climate and AI risks cascade, compound or collide, particularly as public debt and insurance have less capacity to absorb shocks. Boards should map convergence points and dependencies, rehearse compound shocks, assign ownership and crisis decision rights, and fund targeted alternatives that preserve room to act.

articles.title: WHO Launches Global Research Priorities on Climate, Health and Migration
articles.summary: WHO launched a global research-prioritization and action plan on health, migration and displacement in the context of climate change. The plan targets evidence gaps concerning health, well-being and access to care as climate-related mobility affects vulnerable populations.

articles.title: Quadripartite Collaboration Extends the One Health Joint Plan of Action to 2029
articles.summary: FAO, UNEP, WHO and WOAH extended the One Health Joint Plan of Action through 2029. The extension gives countries continuity for planning and scaling national One Health priorities under a shared global framework.

articles.title: World Bank Group: International Development, Poverty and Sustainability
articles.summary: The World Bank Group homepage presents its partnership of 189 member countries and its work on poverty reduction and sustainable development. It provides access to development research, financing initiatives and country programmes.

articles.title: Cambodia SEADRM2 Project Early Market Engagement Workshop
articles.summary: The workshop informs potential bidders about procurement for the second Cambodia Southeast Asia Disaster Risk Management project. It is designed to assess market interest, gather feedback on procurement and support transparent, competitive participation.

articles.title: Nature-Based Solutions Secure Guinea's Water at the Source
articles.summary: The World Bank describes how nature-based solutions are improving water resources and economic conditions in Guinea. The project uses ecosystem-based measures to strengthen water security at its source.

articles.title: Samoa Set to Strengthen Disaster Readiness, Protect Livelihoods and Create Jobs with New World Bank Support
articles.summary: World Bank financing will strengthen Samoa's ability to prepare for, withstand and recover from climate- and disaster-related events. The programme is expected to protect lives and livelihoods for about 180,000 people, or 80% of the population.

articles.title: World Bank Approves US$500 Million to Power Morocco's Jobs and Green Growth Agenda
articles.summary: The World Bank approved a US$500 million development-policy loan for Morocco's employment and green-growth agenda. The financing supports labour-market policy, small and medium-sized firms, clean energy, energy efficiency and export-oriented pharmaceutical industries.

articles.title: World Bank Group Support to Help the Philippines Expand Resilient Water and Sanitation Services
articles.summary: A World Bank Group project will expand safe and reliable water and sanitation services in selected Philippine island provinces. The investment is intended to improve water security, local development, tourism and employment.

articles.title: Advancing the Systems Change Needed to Fight Climate Change
articles.summary: WRI works with policymakers, businesses and civil society to advance systems change for climate action at local, national and international levels. Its climate portal connects research, data and initiatives across policy and economic systems.

articles.title: How Rising Temperatures Could Affect Your City
articles.summary: WRI presents projections for how 1.5°C versus 3°C of global warming could affect nearly 1,000 of the world's largest cities. The comparison makes the local physical consequences of different warming pathways visible for urban planning.

articles.title: India Announces New 2035 Climate Commitment
articles.summary: India's new nationally determined contribution targets a 47% reduction in GDP emissions intensity from 2005 levels by 2035. It also targets a 60% non-fossil share of installed electricity capacity and up to 4 billion tonnes of additional carbon-dioxide-equivalent absorption from forest and tree cover.
